What we are building

ÉTÈ — Eternal Terra Ear — is an independent institute for computational governance. We cast sensor signal, law and city infrastructure into a single instrument: so that power can be audited, and trust can be measured.

01 · The instrument

Signal becomes terrain

Radio-frequency spectrum, latency and telemetry are cast into interactive 3D terrain. You stop reading a report and start walking into the data.

02 · Trust

Geometry is the reasoning

Language is too fragile to govern automated infrastructure. Trust is a distance metric, a boundary check, a topological invariant — certified live.

03 · The incubator

Seeding it back into the world

Each year in Berlin we offer resources first, then co-build with immigrants, minorities, artists and engineers. Research becomes real-world impact.

Register 2 · Systemic

The shape itself is certified

Betti numbers, curvature, hull hash — a certificate over the system's shape, chainable to auditors. A million clean transactions cannot fake a healthy topology.

Evidence registry — /evidence

CASE 001 · IR-2019-11 · recomputed from public telemetry

verified event

On 16 November 2019, following fuel-price protests, Iranian authorities ordered a shutdown: cellular operators disconnected first around 14:00 local, and by 19:00 the country entered digital darkness — international connectivity down to roughly 4–5%. The near-total blackout held until 10:00 on 21 November: 111 hours. During the window, security forces killed at least 304 people; the domestic intranet stayed online. The event is cross-verified by four independent sources: IODA (BGP / active probing / telescope signals), OONI (measurements still arriving from 49 networks — proof the blackout was not total), Google traffic data, and the Amnesty International × Hertie School forensic investigation.

schematic reconstruction anchored to documented signal levels (100% → ~4–5% → recovery); not the raw series. sources: ooni.org/post/2019-iran-internet-blackout · ioda.inetintel.cc.gatech.edu · iran-shutdown.amnesty.org · pulse.internetsociety.org

…

CASE 002 · TO-2022-01 · single-point fragility

verified event

On 15 January 2022, the Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai eruption severed Tonga's only international subsea cable (~827 km to Fiji), cutting nearly all internet connectivity for a population of ~105,000. Mainline repair took about five weeks, restored 22 February; limited satellite links carried government traffic in between. Compiled constraint: critical connectivity requires redundant paths (ITU resilience guidance) — membership test: FAILED — one cable, no redundancy. The case shows fragility becoming a measurable governance fact without any actor violating anything.

Live forensic records · autonomously generated by the agents · C2PA-shaped

The ÉTÈ Incubator · /incubator

Not a conference: a philanthropy-based engine for recruiting seeds. Nov 5–7, 2026 · Berlin Science Week · Motion Lab, Berlin. We offer first, then we co-decide together.

R

Research — one question, four laboratories

How can computational systems remain understandable, contestable and governable as societies shift from legal text to algorithmic infrastructure? Each laboratory holds one face of that question.

The institute is organized as four laboratories, not a collection of disconnected projects. Each lab holds one face of the question: whether geometry can carry governance (Lab 1); whether law can be computed and stay contestable (Lab 2); whether industry and the built environment can answer for their obligations (Lab 3); and whether institutions themselves can be designed and experimented upon (Lab 4). Prototype stages, snapshot data and asserted invariants are labeled on the instrument surface itself.

LAB 1

Geometrical Governance

spatial composition · organizational geometry · topology · satellite systems

Problem: the objects of governance are spatial — orbital slots, spectrum, low-altitude corridors, organizational structures. Method: compile them into checkable geometry: composition, topology, the satellite layer. Instruments: the Landscape Instrument v8 · the Composer & green slope · the trust polytope · the six-window front instrument.

LAB 2

Computational Law

ai auditing · legal complexity · contestability · infrastructure compliance

Problem: obligations are written for humans but enforced against computational systems. Method: compile law into executable audit geometry — compliance as membership test, every breach a signed record. Instruments: the Governance Graph prototype · the trust engine & forensic loop · DSA/AI-Act/CSDDD/co-determination schema pilots · the registry.

LAB 3

Industrial Intelligence

bim · digital twins · construction ai · infrastructure governance

Problem: twins that represent infrastructure do not answer for it. Method: build twins that do — IFC in, codes compiled, agents audit, signed compliance out; the bilingual EU + GB standards library is a capability no one else holds. Current work: the BIM/twin compliance pilot · the OUIM & ISH engines · Beijing BIM-AI field research · AMYGDALA, the encrypted edge-sentinel robotics unit (concept: spatial recognition and alerting that only stores and decodes signals — a witness, never a controller; non-military by design).

LAB 4

Institution Design

collective structures · governance experiments

Problem: institutions are usually inherited, not designed. Method: design collective structures and run governance experiments on them — no slot without a socket, one sandbox case per organization, the three-monies firewall, the never-for-sale registry. Current experiments: the ÉTÈ Incubator & its three sockets · the Bluebook open assembly · the Sandbox · the institute's own governance model.

LAB 5

Cultural Forensics

memorial culture · cybernetic mourning · archival refusal · anthropological forensics

Problem: memory institutions store, but can they mourn? Method: cultural and anthropological forensics — memorial culture, cybernetic mourning, practices of archival refusal; storing what is most human in the most humanless space, and asking how a system ontologically unable to mourn could translate mourning. Current work: the Ritual Memory Datacenter — a memorial drafted collectively.

A·01

Application domain 01 · Nuclear infrastructure governance

Lab 1 · spatialization

Spatializing nuclear infrastructure

Nuclear power plants, waste repositories and fuel supply corridors are not abstract legal text — they are concrete physical space. With GIS and 3D spatial modelling, nuclear governance and its contested data become a contestable spatial surface: a repository siting is an envelope, a safety perimeter a half-space, a transport corridor checkable geometry.

Lab 2 · public auditing

Nuclear data governance & transparency

What the nuclear sector lacks most is comprehensibility and public trust. An open civil-auditing instrument renders safety envelopes, monitoring telemetry and compliance states as objects any citizen can inspect, recompute and contest — squarely on Europe's frontier concern of nuclear safety × public trust × AI digital governance.

status: research direction (Lab 1 × Lab 2) · seeking data & institutional partners · partnership@ete.institute

Applied domain · Lab 1 × Lab 2

Nuclear governance — spatialization & public auditing

The premise: nuclear plants, waste repositories and fuel supply routes are not abstract statutes but concrete physical space — therefore compilable into geometry: siting envelopes, transport corridors, repository topology, a contestable spatial surface. The gap: what the nuclear sector lacks most is public comprehensibility. The institute's open civil-auditing instrument places public telemetry (EURDEP, the European radiological data exchange; IAEA PRIS reactor data) and compiled safety frameworks (Euratom safeguards) in one recomputable model — where civil nuclear safety, public trust and digital governance meet. Civil applications only; military use is excluded at the level of our Terms.

PUBLICATIONS — Methodology (published open at ete.institute; archival DOI pending) · Sovereign Spatial Bluebook (annual; to parliamentary committees Dec 2026) · working-paper series · forensic case reports. FLAGSHIPS — The Instrument (Lab 1) · The ÉTÈ Incubator & Bluebook (Lab 4) · The Open Evidence Registry (Lab 2 · never for sale).
A

About — an independent institute for computational governance

We audit smart cities, IoT and critical infrastructure, drawing on antidisciplinary talent around the globe, and hand over the signed records the instruments produce.

ÉTÈ Institute (Eternal Terra Ear · 永地耳) is an independent research institute for computational governance, fiscally hosted by Open Source Europe in Brussels, working bilingually in English and Chinese across Brussels, Berlin and Beijing. We hold one thesis: as governance migrates from legal text to algorithmic infrastructure, it remains legitimate only if verification is constructive.

Commitment 01

Constructive verification

Every claim we make about a system is backed by a model a third party can run.

Commitment 02

Evidence over assertion

Outputs are cryptographically signed, hash-anchored and archived; methodology published in the open. Our results do not require trusting us.

Commitment 03

Contestability by design

The communities monitored by a model must be able to inspect, recompute and challenge it — a design requirement, not an ethics annex.

INDEPENDENCE & FUNDING — three monies, strictly separated. Sponsorship buys technical embedding (ingestion slots, schema compilation) — never editorial control. Grants fund the commons: the open registry, free audit queries for journalists and human-rights NGOs, bursaries. Investment enters only the service entity — never the protocol or registry, which are held for the commons in perpetuity. The registry is not for sale; that sentence is our governance model. Dual-use here means investigative and commercial — never military.

Isabella Pasqualini
Institute of Visual Narrative · MA Design, Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts
Architect, artist, scientist
Isabella Pasqualini is an architect (ETHZ 2000), artist and scientist working across architecture and cognitive neuroscience (PhD EPFL 2012). She is currently a lecturer at the Institute of Visual Narrative and the MA Design at the Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts. Her works explore the mutual and intimate relationship between body and space through immersive multimedia, with a particular interest in the multisensory enhancement of the user’s horizon. She has been a researcher at the Center of Neuroprosthetics EPFL and the École Nationale Supérieure d’Architecture de Versailles, and a guest lecturer at ZHdK, the Art and Design Academy of Tsinghua University, the School of Engineering and Architecture EPFL and the Städelschule Architecture Class. She has won several international competition prizes and exhibited at international art venues.
Isabel Millar
Philosopher · psychoanalysis and AI
Global Centre for Advanced Studies
“Capacity Reversal Syndrome: On AI and Proletarianization.” Dr Isabel Millar is a philosopher and psychoanalytic theorist from London. She is Professor at the Global Centre for Advanced Studies and author of the critically acclaimed The Psychoanalysis of Artificial Intelligence, so far translated into Chinese, Turkish, Farsi, Spanish, Italian, French, Dutch, German and Arabic. She has been described as one of the UK’s leading young thinkers. Her next book, Patipolitics, is forthcoming with Bloomsbury.
Selena Savić
University of Amsterdam
Artist, architect, assistant professor
“Re-generative Past in AI.” Selena Savić is an artist, architect, and assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam. Her work explores critical and creative approaches to data and its critique at the intersection of informational processes and postcolonial technocracy. She researches, teaches, and writes about digital archives, computational modelling, feminist materialism, and posthuman networks in the context of art, design, and architecture. Her research into the technical, socio-political and environmental aspects of artificial intelligence takes stock of materialist concerns for the ways technology automates performance and creativity, locating a history of measurement in stories of data collection. Rejecting ‘data idealism,’ she studies a proto-history of AI that challenges conventional causalities between technology and society.
Iliana Papadopoulou
Architect · artist · creative developer
Computational media
Iliana Papadopoulou is an architect, artist and creative developer, holding an MArch from Aristotle University and an MSc in Architectural Computation from The Bartlett School of Architecture, UCL. Her teaching and research roles at IAAC, CITA and The Bartlett have served as platforms to rethink computational media through multidisciplinary experimentation. At Henning Larsen in Copenhagen she contributed to R&D projects exploring emerging technologies to shape new spatial experiences, with a focus on local communities and diversity. She currently contributes to open-source software repositories alongside her artistic and theoretical projects, experimenting with game engines, web interfaces, 3D sculpting and creative coding. Her work has been exhibited and published internationally, including at the Media Architecture Biennale in Amsterdam, the Tbilisi Architecture Biennale, and the Royal Danish Academy in Copenhagen.
Natalia Jiménez
XAIA · Women of the Future
Future architect, systems thinker
Natalia is a future architect and one of the most influential voices at the intersection of technology, impact and female leadership in Latin America. As co-founder of Lulo X, she transformed it from a spin-off of Colombia’s first fully digital bank into a fintech recognized for its innovation, inclusion and regenerative vision. Maria da Piedade Ferreira
Hochschule für Technik Stuttgart (HFT) · Corporeal Architecture

Dr. Maria da Piedade Ferreira is an architect, performance artist, researcher and curator. Her doctoral thesis “Embodied Emotions: Observations and Experiments in Architecture and Corporeality” (2016) coins her concept of ‘Corporeal Architecture.’ Her work explores the interconnections between architecture, neuroscience and art and has been published and presented internationally, including at the ANFA, eCAADe and IUAV conferences. In 2020, as a response to COVID-19, she founded the YouTube channel Corporeal Architecture, a curatorial project that works as an open-access education and exhibitions room. She has taught at TU Munich, ETH Zürich, TU Kaiserslautern and HFT Stuttgart.
Alejandro Quinto
Community AI
Designer-strategist
Alejandro Quinto is a designer-strategist who turns messy, territorial data into decision-grade tools for governments, industry and communities. Trained in architecture and working across Europe and the UK, he blends geospatial analytics and AI to make complex systems legible, accountable and actionable — especially where procurement, investment and social value intersect. His portfolio ranges from city-scale data platforms to gamified spatial interfaces that open datasets to non-experts. Mohamed Elshahed
Cairobserver
Independent
Mohamed Elshahed is a writer, curator and critic of architecture whose work extends to design and material culture. He is the author of Cairo Since 1900: An Architectural Guide (AUC Press, 2020) and Rebellious Things: A History of Modern Egypt in Objects, and curated Cairo Modern at New York’s Center for Architecture (2021–22). He earned a Master’s from MIT’s Aga Khan Program for Islamic Architecture and a PhD from NYU’s Department of Middle Eastern Studies, and curates the British Museum’s Modern Egypt Project. Ruba Al-Sweel
Writer · artist · curator
Asia Cultural Centre
“FIRST PHONE” — a film developed by Ruba Al-Sweel, followed by remarks. What is it like to live through climate change and geopolitical unrest from the vantage point of the screen, of platform capitalism and algorithms? As NPCs during epoch-making events, how do we make sense of the apophenic experience of scrolling? Narrated by a disarticulate AI egregore, FIRST PHONE plays like a more-than-human stream of consciousness, decentring humans in its imaginary: text operates as image, metaphor as truth, rhetoric as more than adornment, drawing parallels between the indifferent machine and Red Sea hostilities of political and ecological nature. Ruba Al-Sweel is an independent writer and artist focused on media theory and networked communications.
LAS Art Foundation
Berlin · curatorial speaker: Agnessa Schmudke
R&D as Infrastructure
LAS Art Foundation is an arts organisation that examines the present and gives form to future imaginaries. Collaborating with visionary artists, thinkers and institutions worldwide, LAS realises interdisciplinary projects and experiences that explore topics ranging from artificial intelligence, quantum computing and gaming to ecology and biotechnology, illuminating the intersections of art, science and emerging technologies. Since its inception, LAS has sought to redefine what an arts organisation can be: not only a platform for artistic production and learning but also a site for research and development that, through cross-disciplinary collaboration, interrogates systemic crises — ecological, humanitarian and post-extractivist. Their presentation reflects on how such an institutional model can cultivate resilience and experimentation.
eHTC

Segura in 2023 as a pilot program to test practice-based research methods at the School of Architecture, LCI Veritas (Costa Rica), where it initiated the project Cement Landscapes and Unauthorized Biographies on the environments surrounding the cement industry. Alongside Operaciones (Costa Rica) and Truncata Workshop (USA), eHTC developed an experimental residency under Residencias Remotas at UNAB SoA. It has exhibited and published across units of Geophysics, Philosophy and History (University of Costa Rica), Architecture (UNAB and ETSAM) and Art (UNSAM, Argentina), and has joined Autónomas Forenses, the network of Forensic Architecture agencies in Latin America. Unit members include Carlos A. Segura, Javier Peña (working on 3D clay printing for coral reef regeneration) and Luis Alejandro Sánchez Rivera.
Social Sensibility R&D
Bern · Beijing · Paris
R&D departments

Alessandro is a multidisciplinary artist and researcher based in Bern after 18 years in Beijing, focused on social intervention and decentralized autonomous practices; exhibited at the Venice Biennale, Gwangju Biennale and Manifesta 12, a Roxbourg Fellow and former co-curator of the Beijing Media Art Biennale. Ventures — one motherboard, separated engines

The institute is the substrate; OUIM and ISH are the engines — separated as entities, merged at the substrate. The protocol and the registry never enter the commercial entities.

Engine 01 · design intelligence

OUIM — one vertical design space

City and infrastructure as a twin that answers. The low-altitude economy, designed before it is flown. The satellite layer as a design input. Design outputs that hold up as evidence — including a concept wearable agent: signals and memory accreted, layer by layer, into infra-intelligence. ouim.space ↗

Engine 02 · compliance system

ISH — sovereign sky zero-carbon compliance

Three layers, one computable governance plane. Three regions — no single jurisdiction dominates. One anchor industrial partner per region, co-founding the standard. Deck on request: partnership@ete.institute.

↓

OUIM — the platform, live

GOVERNANCE — both engines sit on the service-entity track (the "investment" money of the three). Design outputs flow back as Composer import files; the evidence layer stays with the institute, neutral, always.
€

Pilots & partners — the service entity

Compliance happens in documents; violations happen in space. What we sell is the evidence layer: continuous, signed, recomputable by any party. The institute stays neutral — the registry is never for sale. Dual-use means investigative and commercial, never military.

Offer 01 · 3 slots

Official Ingestion Partnership

Your telemetry embedded in the Tier 2 anonymized pipeline, running live on the ÉTÈ Incubator main screen; your protocol becomes the 2027 Bluebook baseline. Tooling sponsorship + technical endorsement. Indicative €15–50k.

Offer 02

Schema Compilation

Your framework — AI Act, DSA, CSDDD/LkSG, GB standards — compiled into executable, verifiable audit geometry. Deliverable: schema + live demo + documentation. Indicative €6–20k per framework.

Offer 03

Certified Forensic Audit

Per-certificate signed evidence reports (law firms, compliance, insurers), or continuous-monitoring subscription pilots. Indicative from €2.5k per report; €3–8k/month pilot.

Offer 05 · robotics · concept stage

AMYGDALA · the edge sentinel unit

An embedded robotics module modeled on the amygdala: fast alerting, spatial recognition, threat-salience judgment — for infrastructure sites and vehicles. Fully encrypted end to end; the unit only stores and decodes signals, never commands — a witness, not a controller. Every signal can land as a signed evidence record. Explicitly not applicable to military deployment. Lab 3 R&D · pilot partners: partnership@ete.institute.

Offer 04 · new

BIM / Twin Compliance Pilot

IFC into the Composer → codes compiled as constraint envelopes → agents audit → signed compliance report. Bilingual EU + GB standards library is a capability no one else holds. Indicative from €10k.

The diligence FAQ

How do you make money?

Five lines: ingestion partnerships (€15–50k) · schema compilation (€6–20k/framework) · certified forensic audits (from €2.5k/report; subscriptions €3–8k/mo) · BIM/twin pilots (from €10k) · AMYGDALA units (hardware + decode subscription, concept stage).

Why can't a big firm copy this?

They can copy software; they cannot copy three things: neutrality (a Big-Four auditing itself convinces no one), the accumulated signed-evidence registry, and the bilingual EU+GB standards library. Witness status is structural, not a feature.

Why now?

AI-Act obligations phase in, DSA enforcement accelerates, CSDDD lands — the compliance budgets are approved and the instruments don't exist yet. The regulatory clock is our market clock.

Is the robotics serious?

Serious, and deliberately conservative: AMYGDALA is an encrypted witness unit with zero command authority — which places it in the fastest-to-certify machine class in Europe. Prototype first, certify second, never military (excluded at the level of our Terms).

RITUAL.MEMORY.DATACENTER · NECROPOLIS.INDEX · v0 · 永土耳

Mortality salience is a documented driver of human information behavior: burial, inscription, archiving and transmission operate as loss-mitigation systems. This experiment tests a hypothesis — whether affective content can be preserved in infrastructures that lack affect, and what is lost in the translation.

Method — Corpus: documentary footage of funerals, mourning and burial rites. Index structure: a spatialized necropolis topology (traversable, enterable chambers). Interaction protocol: traverse, focus, step inside. Metadata schema: time, place, rite type per death event. The system is designed to keep operating unattended — not as metaphor but as experimental condition.

RQ 1

Storage ≠ mourning

The act of storing derives from loss aversion and is therefore a human trait; the storage infrastructure itself does not participate in mourning. Distinguishing the two is the experiment's first measurement.

RQ 2

Machine thanatology

Technical systems have their own termination modes: expired credentials, unresolvable links, decommissioned servers, unreadable formats. Operational death can be formally defined and indexed — the experiment places it beside the metadata of biological death.

RQ 3

Limits of translation

A data center preserves traces of death through technical operations — metadata, redundancy, checksums — rather than ritual: preservation without mourning. The core question is thus statable precisely: which properties of mourning can a system ontologically unable to mourn preserve, and which are lost?

Case method — Practices of archival refusal as research object: refusing what has been refused to us; anti-generalisation; working in case series and essays. The series spans successive revolutionary periods: grassroots archives created, appropriated, and reconstructed.

THE BUILD BELOW IS THE ARTIFACT ITSELF, UNSIMPLIFIED. CONTENT NOTE — documentary footage of funerals and mourning rites. CONTROLS — ← → traverse · click to focus · ENTER step inside · WASD walk · ESC leave.

Privacy notice

No cookies, no trackers, no analytics. This website does not know who you are.

Controller: ÉTÈ Institute, fiscally hosted by Open Source Europe, Brussels. Contact: partnership@ete.institute.

What we do not collect: this site sets no cookies, loads no third-party tracking or analytics, and keeps no visitor logs of its own. All 3D rendering happens locally in your browser.

Local storage: only internal tool pages use your browser's localStorage to keep working state (pipeline state; the dismissal of this notice). The data lives on your device only and can be cleared in your browser at any time.

Third-party requests: the three.js library loads from cdnjs.cloudflare.com; the Landscape Instrument page, when opened, makes anonymous read-only requests to public data APIs (OONI, GDELT) to display live signals. Nothing else leaves your device.

Email: anything you send to partnership@ete.institute is used solely to answer your request (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)), is not shared with third parties, and is deleted on request.

Your rights: under the GDPR you may access, correct, erase, and lodge a complaint (Belgian DPA: autoriteprotectiondonnees.be).

V2

The next horizon — evidence-based spatial intelligence

From civic evidence instrument to an autonomous, privacy-preserving Spatial AI Agent — one that doesn't synthesize prose, but reasons through sovereign 3D spatial telemetry.

[ Raw multilayer telemetry ] │ ▼ [ Tier 2 · Tokenization engine ] ──▸ strips identities · secures local actors │ ▼ [ Spatial AI reasoning core ] ──▸ interrogates BGP, RF & structural networks │ ▼ [ Cryptographic output · C2PA ] ──▸ signed, verifiable semantic geometries
R&D 01

Autonomous forensic reasoning

A 7×24 digital detective: continuously monitors transnational datasets (OONI, OpenSky, IODA) and flags correlation anomalies without human instruction — a localized BGP hijack overlapping unexpected low-altitude airspace restrictions.

R&D 02

Geometric spatial intelligence

Beyond LLMs into spatial computing: line-of-sight propagation, path-loss vectors for radio interference, volumetric cross-border flows — materialized as immutable 3D objects. Attacks are not virtual; they land on cables, base stations, beams.

R&D 03

Privacy-preserving edge auditing

Cryptographic tokenization and zero-knowledge principles at ingestion: audits state-level network threats and physical infrastructure vulnerabilities while mathematically guaranteeing the anonymity of individual citizens inside attack zones.

Theoretical ground · Ruffini & Castaldo, Pattern, Persist! (2026)

Algorithmic persistence: a compressed identity that survives the filter of time

Our agents follow the algorithmic agent's triad — a Modeling Engine, a scalar Objective Function, a Planning Engine: model-mediated regulation. Every C2PA manifest is exactly that "compressed identity"; every boundary check is an irreversible act of regulation across a thin, thermodynamically costly boundary (its Landauer cost is the price of trust). By the Algorithmic Regulator Theorem, a regulator shares mutual algorithmic information with what it regulates — an auditor must contain a model of the audited. This is why the evidence must persist with the instrument. (external reference: Ruffini & Castaldo, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.21278422, CC-BY 4.0 — not an ÉTÈ publication)

Step one is complete: geometric semantic modelling. Next: giving this geometric world the spatial intelligence to reason and to resist forgery. The technical architecture whitepaper launches on Day 3 of the ÉTÈ Incubator.
